title: This Reptile Has a Third Eye and No Living Relatives
subject: tuatara

scenes.text: This reptile has a third eye on top of its head. And its whole family is gone.
It's the tuatara of New Zealand, from a group that lived alongside the dinosaurs.
All but one species in that group died out about 60 million years ago. The tuatara is the survivor.
The third eye has a lens and a retina and can sense light, though a scale covers it in adults.
It likes body temperatures of 60 to 70 degrees Fahrenheit, the coolest of any reptile.
Everything about it is slow: about 14 years to mature, and well over a hundred years of life.

description:
The tuatara has a light-sensing third eye on top of its head and is the lone survivor of a group that walked with the dinosaurs.
It prefers the coolest body temperatures of any reptile and can live over 100 years.
What other living fossil should we cover?
first_comment: A third eye that senses light, hidden under a scale. What would you do with one?
